full_judgment: 2. Relevant facts are: Upon a prosecution report dated 25-2-97 submitted by a Sub-inspector of Police. Mizanur Rahman pursuant to GD entry No. 1079 dated 20-2-97, of Cantonment Police Station, Dhaka in respect of CS Plot No. 58 appertaining to CS Khatian No. 138. Mouza Kafrul, Dhaka city, and in pursuance of the applications filed in respect of the said plot of land, one by Alhaj Abul Bashar (petitioners in Criminal Petition Nos. 8 and 9 of 1998) and other by Mr Abu Salek(petitioner in Criminal Petition No. 10/98) as first party, under section 145 CrPC, the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka on 25-2-97, 10-12- 96 and 19-12-96 respectively drew up those three proceedings against respondent No. 1 Hasanuddin Ahmed and others asking them to show cause as to why such proceedings would not be drawn as claimed. Accordingly in two cases the local Officer-in-Charge of the Police Station was directed to maintain law and order in respect of the proceeding land. But in respect of the subject matter of Criminal Petition No. 8 of 1998, the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate however appointed an Assistant Police Commissioner, Uttara PS as its receiver, pending disposal of the said proceeding. In all those proceedings respondent No. 1 Hasanuddin Ahmed as the 2nd party filed written statement opposing initiation of those proceedings under section 145 CrPC stating, inter alia, that the aforesaid petitioner Abul Bashar Chowdhury has already filed Title Suit No. 216 of 1994 in the 3rd Court of Subordiante Judge, Dhaka for partitioning the disputed plot claiming his share of 0.036 acres out of a total area of 0.69 acres and in that suit the order of maintaining status quo, passed on 4-10-95, has been in force and that Abu Salek (petitioner in Criminal Petition No. 10/98) has also instituted Title Suit No. 122 of 1996 against the said Hasanuddin Ahmed and others in the 3rd Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for declaration of his title to and recovery of possession of 0.065 acres of the land out of said disputed plot and in that suit also an order of maintaining status quo, passed on 23-11-96, has been in force. Accordingly, it was contended that the possession of the disputed plot having already been regulated by the civil Court the criminal proceedings under section 145 should be dropped.
